name: Football · Rules
description: Recall the Laws of the Game and the words used on the pitch: the numbers, the restarts, the cards and the terms.

cards.front: Beyond the second-last defender when a teammate passes: which offence?
cards.label: law
cards.hook: Law 11 of the Laws of the Game.

cards.front: How far is the penalty spot from the goal line?
cards.label: distance
cards.hook: The spot sits in line with the centre of the goal.

cards.front: How deep is the penalty area from each goal line?
cards.label: distance
cards.hook: The penalty arc is 10 yards (9.1 m) from the spot.

cards.front: How many players does each team have on the pitch?
cards.label: players
cards.hook: Two teams of 11 players each.

cards.front: Fewer than how many players and the match should stop?
cards.label: players
cards.hook: IFAB recommends stopping a match below seven players.

cards.front: How long is a standard match in regulation time?
cards.label: time
cards.hook: Two halves of 45 minutes each.

cards.front: How long is each extra-time period?
cards.label: time
cards.hook: Extra time is two periods, 30 minutes in all.

cards.front: How many kicks does each side take first in a shoot-out?
cards.label: shoot-out
cards.hook: Each kick must be taken by a different player.

cards.front: Substitutions allowed in a 90-minute league game?
cards.label: substitutes
cards.hook: One more is allowed if the game goes into extra time.

cards.front: What does VAR stand for?
cards.label: technology
cards.hook: It reviews decisions using video footage and advises the referee.

cards.front: Which rule lets play go on when the fouled side will benefit?
cards.label: rule
cards.hook: The referee waits a few seconds to see whether the benefit comes.

cards.front: Which free kick cannot be scored from directly?
cards.label: free kick
cards.hook: The referee keeps an arm raised until another player touches the ball.

cards.front: Which rule stops a goalkeeper handling a teammate's deliberate kick?
cards.label: rule
cards.hook: Law 12, Section 2 of the Laws of the Game.

cards.front: Which card is shown for a caution?
cards.label: card

cards.front: What happens to a player who receives a second caution?
cards.label: card
cards.hook: A second yellow card is followed by a red card.

cards.front: A goal scored into your own net is called what?
cards.label: goal
cards.hook: It counts for the opposing team.

cards.front: Three goals by one player in a single match?
cards.label: term

cards.front: A match in which a team concedes no goals?
cards.label: term
cards.hook: Called a shutout in the United States.

cards.front: A ball played between an opponent's legs?
cards.label: skill
cards.hook: Often used to get behind a defender while dribbling.

cards.front: What decides a knockout match still level after extra time?
cards.label: shoot-out
cards.hook: Shoot-outs end as soon as one team has an insurmountable lead.

cards.front: Three trophies won by one club in one season?
cards.label: term
cards.hook: A continental treble adds the continental trophy to the league and cup.

cards.front: What is the restart at the start of each half?
cards.label: restart
cards.hook: Governed by Law 8 of the Laws of the Game.

cards.front: Defenders touched it last over their own goal line: restart?
cards.label: restart
cards.hook: Taken from the corner nearest to where the ball crossed the line.

cards.front: Where must a goal kick be taken from?
cards.label: restart
cards.hook: The goal area is also called the six-yard box.

cards.front: How must a throw-in be taken?
cards.back: Both hands, from behind and over the head
cards.label: restart
cards.hook: Part of each foot stays on the touchline or outside it.

cards.front: Which restart follows a stoppage that is not a foul or misconduct?
cards.label: restart
cards.hook: Set out in Laws 8 and 9 of the Laws of the Game.

cards.front: What is awarded for a direct-free-kick offence in your penalty area?
cards.label: restart
cards.hook: Taken from the penalty spot, 11 metres from the goal line.
